confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on one web search of cost-of-living sites. Most figures come from a Numbeo-cited Expatica page dated June 2026, cross-checked against Citycost, MyLifeElsewhere, Whereandwhen and Rewireabroad. I converted euros to US dollars at about 1.10 USD per EUR. I took that rate from a third-party page quoting RBA cross rates for 18 Nov 2026; it is not an official RBA EUR/USD figure. I raised beer, coffee and meal prices slightly because July is peak season in this gateway town for the Cinque Terre. I did not search for cocktail or wine prices. I estimated them from the local relationship to beer prices and typical prices on the Ligurian coast (cocktail about €9–10, glass of wine about €5), so these two are less certain. Accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. They reflect strong July demand from Cinque Terre visitors and only a few hostels in the city, so they are the least certain anchors and could be off by 25–35%.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared La Spezia with mid-sized coastal cities in northern and central Italy, such as Livorno and Genoa, for restaurant prices. For summer accommodation I added a premium for peak season near the Cinque Terre.
